questions.text: The notes say that if a payment never gets an outcome, Payment polls the provider after about 35 minutes, but this is left out of the diagram. What does that poll do with the result, and what happens to the order until then?

answers.text: Place order returns once the reserve step finishes: either the short-item list, a try-again message, or an order id. With an order id the browser shows processing and polls Order's status until CONFIRMED, PAYMENT_FAILED or CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK. Emails give the same news. Added a 'What the customer sees' section and END_WAIT in the diagram. Polling is my choice, chosen over push because it needs no extra infrastructure.

Added a PAID order state. Order saves PAID when PaymentSucceeded arrives, then calls claim. On error or timeout it stays PAID and Order retries with backoff, since claim is idempotent per order id, and alerts if it keeps failing. Only a real 'claim failed' answer triggers the refund. Money stays held meanwhile. Retry limits are not chosen and are listed as open.

Order retries the reserve call a few times with the same order id. If it still fails, the order becomes FAILED_UNAVAILABLE, Order sends an idempotent release in case the reply was lost, and the customer is told to try again. A sweeper in Order handles orders stuck PENDING after a crash. Added to the diagram and step 2. Exact counts and time limits are not chosen and are listed as open.
The arrow was wrong. The sweeper only moves ACTIVE holds past 10 minutes to EXPIRED and triggers nothing. I removed the arrow and labelled the sweeper as standalone.

'Cancelled' was misleading: the only cancel state is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, now stated explicitly. A success for an order not AWAITING_PAYMENT should not happen, so this is a defensive branch. Repeats for orders already PAID, CONFIRMED or CANCELLED are ignored. Otherwise Order requests a refund with reason UNEXPECTED_PAYMENT, keeps the status unchanged and sends a non-stock email. You were right that stock-gone was the wrong reason, so the diagram has a separate node O7B.

StockReserved carries order id, total and currency, and Payment uses those for the charge. Payment stores the provider payment id, and the webhook carries it, so Payment maps webhook to payment to order id. The provider event id is generated by the provider and repeated on re-delivery. That the webhook contains both fields is an assumption I could not verify, so it is listed as an open question to check against provider docs.

Release changes only an ACTIVE reservation to RELEASED. In EXPIRED, CLAIMED or RELEASED it is a no-op that replies ok. If Inventory is unreachable, Order keeps retrying, and the 10 minute expiry frees the stock anyway if that never succeeds. Now in step 6 and the I5 node.

Order generates the order id. A checkout token is made in the browser when the checkout page loads (and renewed after a failure), sent through Cart to Order, and stored under a unique constraint, so a repeated token returns the existing order. Gap: two tabs with different tokens can create two orders. I accepted that and noted it in the document.

Order stores the cart id, and OrderConfirmed carries the cart id and the ordered lines. Cart removes exactly those lines and quantities, so items added during the wait stay. This slightly narrows 'emptied' from the brief, so I flagged it as a decision you may change.

Added the poller to the diagram and as step 11. After 35 minutes in PENDING, Payment asks the provider for the outcome and runs it through the same declined or succeeded path as a webhook. A payment leaves PENDING only once, so a poll and a late webhook cannot both act. Still pending means ask again and alert. The order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT until then. What to do if the provider has no record of the charge is not decided and is listed as an open question.

questions.text: What happens if the charge request from Payment to the provider errors or times out? Does anything retry it, and what state is the payment in?
questions.about: Create payment PENDING -> charge request -> Payment provider

questions.text: Order saves PAID and then calls claim. If Order crashes between those two, what restarts the claim? The sweeper described only covers PENDING orders.
questions.about: Order PAID - money is held, call Inventory to claim

questions.text: Consumers tolerate duplicates, but OrderConfirmed removes quantities from the cart. If it is delivered twice, how does Cart avoid removing the lines twice?
questions.about: Remove the ordered lines and quantities from the cart

questions.text: Where does Order record that a refund is done? The order states list has no refund state, and the node only says 'Record refund as done'.
questions.about: Record refund as done / email customer: refund complete

questions.text: The browser polls for status. Which statuses does it see for an order with PAID or AWAITING_PAYMENT, and what does the customer see if the poll is still running after the 10-minute hold has lapsed?
questions.about: Browser shows processing and polls the order status

questions.text: How does the cart get from the browser to Cart's 'Snapshot' step, and what does Cart do if the HTTP call to Order fails or times out? Does the browser's retry with the same token cover that?
questions.about: HTTP: create order with snapshot and token

questions.text: When the claim finds a lapsed hold and re-takes the stock, what if only the reservation is RELEASED or the order was already FAILED_UNAVAILABLE and released? Can a claim ever arrive for a reservation in the RELEASED state, and what does it answer?
questions.about: Reservation still ACTIVE? / Expired: can ALL lines be taken again now?

answers.text: Payment keeps the payment PENDING and retries the same request with the same idempotency key (order id) with backoff, so a charge that did go through is not repeated. At the retry limit it alerts, and the 35-minute poller then asks the provider for the outcome. Added node P1B and text in step 4. Unknown/open: whether a definitive provider rejection counts as declined, and whether the provider can look up a charge by idempotency key when we never got a provider payment id. Both listed as open questions.

Nothing restarted it; that was a hole. Added an Order sweeper (node OS, step 7) that runs every minute, finds orders PAID for more than a few minutes and retries the claim, which is safe because the claim is keyed by order id. It is the same sweeper that handles stuck PENDING orders. Time limit not chosen, listed as open.

Cart records handled order ids in a handled-order table, written in the same transaction as the line removal. A second OrderConfirmed finds the id and does nothing. OrderConfirmed now carries the order id too. Added to C9, step 8, the stores table and the how-to-read notes.

Order has a separate refund field (NONE or REFUNDED) rather than a new status, so the status list and the customer-visible final statuses stay unchanged. Node O8 sets it when RefundSucceeded arrives, and a repeat sets the same value and sends no second email. Added to the order states section, step 10 and the stores table.

PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT and PAID all show 'processing, payment confirmation can take up to 30 minutes, we will email you', and polling continues. The hold lapsing changes nothing visible, since the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT until an outcome exists. Added a status-to-display table in 'What the customer sees'. The wording of the message is my choice.

The browser calls Cart's Place order endpoint with the token, and Cart finds the cart from the customer's login session. That authentication detail is an assumption not covered in the brief, now listed as open. If Cart's call to Order fails, Cart retries with the same token a few times, then tells the browser to try again, and the browser's retry reuses the same token, which is safe because Order returns the existing order. I also fixed a contradiction: the token is kept when no answer came back and renewed only after a final answer (short, declined, cancelled, FAILED_UNAVAILABLE), since reusing it would just return that finished order.

It should not happen: only a declined payment or a failed reserve call releases, and neither can lead to PAID, so a claim never normally reaches a RELEASED reservation. If it somehow does, the customer has paid, so I treat RELEASED like EXPIRED: re-take the lines if all are free, otherwise claim failed and refund. A repeat claim on an already CLAIMED reservation replies 'claimed' without changes. Updated step 7 and the I6/I7 nodes. This is a defensive choice, not tested against any existing Inventory behaviour.

questions.text: When Order creates the order and then calls Inventory to reserve, which comes first for the customer: does Order wait for the reserve reply before answering Cart? And the diagram shows StockReserved published at the same time as the HTTP reply to Place order. Is the event written to the outbox in the same transaction as AWAITING_PAYMENT, and what happens if that publish is delayed?
questions.about: Order AWAITING_PAYMENT / publish StockReserved / HTTP reply to Place order

questions.text: What exactly is the 'outbox' and what process reads it and publishes to the broker? What does the broker do if a consumer is down, and how does a consumer get an event again?
questions.about: Every event is written to the sender's own database ... (a transactional outbox)

questions.text: The Order sweeper treats a PENDING order 'as reserve call failed' and sends release. But the reserve may have actually succeeded and the original request may still be running. Could the sweeper mark FAILED_UNAVAILABLE while the original flow is moving the same order to AWAITING_PAYMENT? Which one wins?
questions.about: Order sweeper every minute / PENDING for more than a few minutes

questions.text: If the reserve call failed and the order is FAILED_UNAVAILABLE and released, but a charge somehow was requested or a StockReserved event was already published, what happens? Can StockReserved exist for an order that later becomes FAILED_UNAVAILABLE?
questions.about: Reserve call failed after retries / Order FAILED_UNAVAILABLE

questions.text: What happens to the customer's payment if the provider reports success for a payment whose order is PAYMENT_FAILED or FAILED_UNAVAILABLE? Does the flow always reach O7B, and how does Order learn the amount to refund (the document says full refund)?
questions.about: Order still AWAITING_PAYMENT? -> No -> Order status stays as it is (UNEXPECTED_PAYMENT)

questions.text: How does Payment decide a payment is 'declined' versus an error? What does the provider return for a charge, and what does the customer actually pay with (card details, a saved method)? Where does the payment method come from, since StockReserved only has total and currency?
questions.about: Create payment PENDING / send charge request with total and currency

questions.text: How does Order know to send a claim or order emails only once when PaymentSucceeded or other events are delivered twice? Which steps check state before acting, and what does Order do with a duplicate PaymentSucceeded when the order is already PAID but the claim has not yet completed?
questions.about: PaymentSucceeded -> Order still AWAITING_PAYMENT? / OrderConfirmed email

questions.text: What is the manual queue for REFUND_FAILED, who works it, and what does 'a person closes it' do to the order and the refund record? Also, how does a refund reach the customer's payment method when the order was never CONFIRMED?
questions.about: Refund REFUND_FAILED / alert on-call, add to manual queue

answers.text: Yes. Order waits for Inventory's reserve reply before answering Cart, so the Place order reply is short items, try again, or the order id. AWAITING_PAYMENT and the StockReserved outbox row are written in the same transaction; a relay publishes it. If the publish is delayed, payment just starts later and the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT; a lapsed hold is handled by the claim step. Stated in the how-to-read notes, step 2, step 4 and the customer section.

The outbox is a table in the sender's own database. A relay process in each service reads unpublished rows, publishes them to the broker and marks them published, so a crash cannot lose an event. For consumers being down I assumed the broker keeps events per subscriber and redelivers until acknowledged (at least once), so consumers must tolerate duplicates. I have not verified our broker does this, so it is listed as an open question.

Yes, they could race, so I made every state change a conditional update that applies only if the record is still in the expected old state (for example PENDING to AWAITING_PAYMENT). Whichever commits first wins and the other sees zero rows changed and stops. If the sweeper wins, the original flow publishes nothing and sends a harmless release. The sweeper's PENDING limit must be longer than the whole reserve retry window, so it should rarely fire on a live request. Added to how-to-read and step 2.

No. StockReserved is written in the same transaction as the PENDING to AWAITING_PAYMENT update, and FAILED_UNAVAILABLE is also set only from PENDING. Only one of the two updates can apply, so the event and FAILED_UNAVAILABLE are mutually exclusive. No charge is requested for a FAILED_UNAVAILABLE order. Stated in step 4.

A success for PAYMENT_FAILED goes to O7B and a refund with reason UNEXPECTED_PAYMENT. A success for FAILED_UNAVAILABLE or REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK cannot happen because no charge is requested for those. Order does not need the amount: RefundRequested carries the order id and Payment refunds the full amount of the payment it already holds for that order id. Added to step 7, step 9, the decisions list and node P8.

Declined means the provider reported a decline by webhook (or poll). An error or timeout on a request is not a decline; it is retried with the same key. This is now said in step 5. Where the payment method comes from is unknown: the brief does not describe it, StockReserved carries only total and currency, and I did not design it. I listed it as an open question, with a guess that the provider holds the method via a token from the browser, not as a decision.

Every Order transition is a conditional update, and only the update that really changed the status queues the next event or email. A second PaymentSucceeded finds PAID (or later) and is ignored. If the order is PAID with the claim unfinished, the claim retry loop or the sweeper is already responsible for it, so the repeat does nothing. The claim call itself is keyed by order id, so repeating it is harmless. The mail sender may rarely deliver an email twice; I accepted that. Added to step 7 and an Emails note.

Not known and not decided: who works the manual queue, what the queue physically is, and what closing a REFUND_FAILED does to the refund record and the order refund field. I did not invent an answer; it is now an open question and step 10 says so. For the second part, the refund is made against the provider payment found by order id, and the provider returns the money to the original payment method, so it does not matter that the order was never CONFIRMED. That is stated in step 9; I did not verify it against the provider's refund API.

questions.text: The first call from the browser to Cart is a Place order request. What does Cart do with a checkout token if the cart is empty or Cart itself crashes after calling Order but before replying to the browser? What does the browser see on retry?
questions.about: START -> Snapshot cart lines and prices

questions.text: How does Order learn the charge outcome is declined or succeeded in the case where Order gets PaymentSucceeded while the order is still PENDING (for example the sweeper has not yet moved it, or the relay delivered events oddly)? Which branch of 'Order still AWAITING_PAYMENT?' does it take?
questions.about: Order still AWAITING_PAYMENT? -> No -> Order status stays as it is

questions.text: When Order sends the release after the reserve call fails, or after the sweeper wins, what happens if that release itself fails? Is it retried like the release after a decline, and by what?
questions.about: Reserve call failed after retries -> send release

questions.text: The claim re-takes stock for an EXPIRED reservation. Is the result a new reservation row or the same row going back to ACTIVE/CLAIMED, and how does it stay keyed by order id when a retry arrives after it already succeeded?
questions.about: EXPIRED or RELEASED: can ALL lines be taken again now?

questions.text: Inventory's section lists an outbox, but no Inventory event appears in the diagram. What does Inventory publish, or is the outbox unused? Also, who tells Order that a claim happened: only the HTTP reply?
questions.about: INVENTORY service - stores table (Inventory outbox)

questions.text: The Payment poller asks the provider for the outcome when the payment is PENDING after 35 minutes. If the charge request never returned a provider payment id and a webhook then arrives, how does Payment match it to a payment?
questions.about: Poller every minute: payment still PENDING after 35 min

questions.text: How does the RefundRequested event for UNEXPECTED_PAYMENT or OUT_OF_STOCK avoid creating two refund records if it is delivered twice? What is the refund idempotency key based on and where is the dedupe done?
questions.about: Refund record REFUND_PENDING / find the payment by order id

answers.text: Empty cart: Cart replies 'cart is empty' and stops; no order, nothing sent to Order. If Cart crashes after calling Order but before replying, the browser gets no answer and retries with the same token; Cart snapshots the unchanged cart again and Order returns the existing order's current result instead of a second order. I also spelled out what a repeated token returns: order id for AWAITING_PAYMENT or later, the stored short-item list for REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, 'try again' for FAILED_UNAVAILABLE or a still-running PENDING. This required storing the short-item list on the order. Added to the customer section, step 1, step 3, C1, O1, O2 and the stores table.

It cannot normally happen: StockReserved is written in the same transaction as PENDING to AWAITING_PAYMENT, so no charge exists while an order is PENDING. If it ever did, it takes the 'No' branch (not AWAITING_PAYMENT), so it goes to O7B and a refund with reason UNEXPECTED_PAYMENT. Stated in steps 4 and 7 and in node O7B. This is a defensive choice, not tested against real behaviour.

Yes, it is retried by Order with backoff until Inventory replies ok, same as the release after a decline. If Order crashes before it succeeds, or it never succeeds, the 10-minute expiry frees the stock, so the worst case is stock held a few minutes longer. Added to step 2, node O2B and a new O2B to I5 arrow.

The same reservation row, one row per order id, goes from EXPIRED or RELEASED to CLAIMED in one transaction that also deducts all lines; no new row is created. A retry after success finds CLAIMED and replies 'claimed' without changes. Stated in step 7 and nodes I4 and I8. Whether the row is unique on order id in the real Inventory stub is not verified.

The Inventory outbox was unused, so I removed it. Inventory publishes no events. Order learns of a reserve, claim or release only from the HTTP reply. Updated the outbox note, the INVENTORY subgraph title, step 7 and the stores table.

Not known. The design matches a webhook through the provider payment id, so if the charge request never returned one, matching is undefined. A possible fix is for the provider to echo the idempotency key or metadata (the order id) in the webhook, but I do not know the provider supports that. I did not invent a rule; it is now an open question and step 5 says so.

Payment keeps at most one refund record per order id, enforced by a unique constraint, because one order has one payment and a full refund. A second RefundRequested finds the record and does nothing, so dedupe is done in Payment's own database. The provider idempotency key is 'refund + order id', identical on every retry, so even a retry cannot refund twice at the provider. Added to the duplicates note, node P8, steps 9 and 10 and the stores table. If one order could legitimately need two refunds (for example partial refunds) this would need rethinking, but the brief only has full refunds.

questions.text: P8 says that if a refund record already exists, stop. But the retry arrow goes from P12 back to P8, where the REFUND_PENDING record already exists. What does a retry actually do at P8, and what starts it (a timer, a stored retry time)?
questions.about: P12 Retry limit reached? -> No -> P8 Refund record REFUND_PENDING

questions.text: The provider payment id is stored after the charge request returns. Could a webhook arrive before Payment has stored that id, for example if the charge reply was slow? How does Payment find the payment then?
questions.about: P1 Create payment PENDING / store provider payment id / P2 Webhook received

questions.text: Is the payment status change, the dedupe insert and the PaymentSucceeded outbox row written in one transaction? And when the poller gets the outcome, which dedupe or conditional update stops it and a webhook from both publishing?
questions.about: P7 Payment SUCCEEDED / publish PaymentSucceeded

questions.text: How does the browser poll Order for the status? Does it call Order directly or go through Cart, and what does it send to identify the order and prove it belongs to this customer?
questions.about: What the customer sees: polls Order for the status

questions.text: What if the payment declines or the order is cancelled, but PaymentSucceeded then arrives after Order has set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK for a different reason? Also, what is the exact update that moves PAID to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and is the RefundRequested event written in the same transaction?
questions.about: O7 Order CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK / I9 Claim failed

answers.text: The P12 to P8 arrow was wrong: a retry must not go through the event handler, which would stop at the existing record. I split P8 in two. P8 only runs on RefundRequested and creates the unique REFUND_PENDING record with an attempt count and next-retry time. New node P8B, a refund retrier timer in Payment (every minute, and once right after the record is created), picks records REFUND_PENDING or REFUND_FAILED whose next-retry time has passed and re-sends the stored request. P12 No and P13 now point at P8B. Step 10 and the stores table say this. The timer interval and backoff are not chosen (open).

Yes, a webhook could arrive before the provider payment id is stored. Rule I chose: Payment finds no payment, stores nothing (not even the event id) and replies with an error, so a provider that re-sends tries again later. Fallback is the 35-minute poller. I do not know whether the provider re-sends after an error reply, nor how matching works if the charge reply never returned an id; both are in the open questions. Added to P2, step 5 and the decisions list.

Yes for the webhook path: one transaction holds the dedupe insert, the conditional update PENDING to SUCCEEDED or DECLINED, and the outbox row. For the poller there is no event id, so the guard is the conditional update from PENDING: whichever of poller and webhook commits first publishes, the other's update changes nothing and it publishes nothing (a webhook then still replies 200). Added to P6, P7, step 5 and step 11.

The browser calls Order directly with the order id and the login session; this is my design choice. To prove ownership, Cart now sends the customer id in the create-order call, Order stores it, and the status endpoint answers only if the session's customer id matches, otherwise 'not found'. The order id is also unguessable. How Order validates the session is not known (the brief has no authentication), so that is an open question. Added to the customer section, step 1, O1, C1 edge and the stores table.

CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK can only be reached from PAID after a real 'claim failed' reply, so there is no other reason for it. A later PaymentSucceeded for such an order is a repeat of the one that made it PAID and is ignored (now stated in step 7). Payment also never publishes both PaymentDeclined and PaymentSucceeded for one payment because a payment leaves PENDING only once. The exact update is: set status CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK where status is PAID, and in the same transaction write RefundRequested (reason OUT_OF_STOCK, order id) and the email to the outbox; if the update changes nothing, nothing is written. Added to step 9 and node O7.

questions.text: Order handles PaymentSucceeded and then calls Inventory to claim. What does Order do with a PaymentDeclined event if the order is not AWAITING_PAYMENT (for example already PAID or FAILED_UNAVAILABLE)? Is O4 also a conditional update?
questions.about: O4 Order PAYMENT_FAILED / PaymentDeclined

questions.text: What exactly does the Order sweeper do when it finds a PENDING order older than the reserve retry window? Does it call Inventory to find out whether the reserve actually succeeded, or does it always mark FAILED_UNAVAILABLE and release?
questions.about: Order sweeper every minute / PENDING for longer than all reserve retries

questions.text: Between PAID and the claim reply, the customer sees 'processing'. If the claim fails and the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, how does the browser's poll or the customer learn that if they have closed the page? Is the email the only channel?
questions.about: Order CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK / What the customer sees

questions.text: What does the customer's status poll return for an order in CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK or PAYMENT_FAILED after the refund field is REFUNDED? Does the refund field appear in what the browser shows?
questions.about: Set the order's refund field to REFUNDED / What the customer sees table

questions.text: After PAYMENT_FAILED, the customer is told they can try again with a new token. Does a retry create a completely new order with a new reservation, and what happens to the old order and its payment?
questions.about: END_DECL / Status poll shows PAYMENT_FAILED

questions.text: The relay marks an outbox row published after sending it to the broker. If the relay crashes after sending but before marking, the event is sent again. Is that the reason consumers must handle duplicates, and how often does the relay run?
questions.about: Outbox relay process

questions.text: The 'handled-order table' in Cart and the dedupe table in Payment record ids. Are these ever cleaned up, and how long must an id be kept to be safe against redelivery?
questions.about: Handled-order table / webhook dedupe table

answers.text: Yes, O4 is a conditional update: set PAYMENT_FAILED where status is still AWAITING_PAYMENT. If it changes nothing the event is a repeat and is ignored; only the update that changed the order sends the release. PAID/CONFIRMED cannot occur because one payment leaves PENDING once and never publishes both outcomes, and FAILED_UNAVAILABLE/REJECTED orders never have a payment. Added to step 6 and node O4. The release is covered by retry plus the 10 minute expiry.

It always marks the order FAILED_UNAVAILABLE (conditional, only if still PENDING) and sends the release. It does not ask Inventory. Reason: release is harmless if nothing was reserved, and asking adds a new call and failure case. Cost: a reservation that did succeed is discarded and the customer retries. Stated in step 2, node OS and the decisions list.

The email is the only pushed message. If the page is closed, the status stays on the order and can be read later with the same status request, since it is stored on the order, not the browser. Added to the customer section. I have not designed an order-history page; that is assumed.

My choice: the status reply includes the refund field. CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK shows 'refund on its way' while NONE and 'refund complete' once REFUNDED; PAYMENT_FAILED with REFUNDED (rare unexpected payment) adds a refunded note. The status table now has a refund column. The wording is my choice.

Yes, a retry after a final answer uses a new token and creates a completely new order: new order id, fresh cart snapshot, new reservation and payment. The old order stays PAYMENT_FAILED with its payment DECLINED and hold released, and nothing further happens to it. Added to the customer section and END_DECL.

Yes, that crash window is one reason for duplicates, since the event is sent again after restart; at-least-once broker delivery is the other. Now said in the outbox note. How often the relay runs is not chosen and I do not know a defensible value; it is added to the open questions (it only affects delay).

Not decided. An id must be kept at least as long as the broker can redeliver the event (Cart) or the provider can re-send the webhook (Payment), and I do not know either period. For now nothing deletes them; the rows are small. Added to the duplicates note and the open questions.
